column2: If repentance requires facing oneself wholly as part of God's creation, and what facing requires is bounded by what one can know of oneself, then repentance is fulfilled only as far as one can see oneself, and is reopened whenever one comes to see more.
Under the definition of sin as remaining turned away, after understanding, from the work of one's own hand, turning away from oneself is sin only insofar as one is the work of one's own hand.
Repentance that faces one's works but not oneself can contain sin's contrary while remaining unfulfilled as repentance.
